title: IngestBatchEnvelope
description: The push-contract request envelope, per architecture.md §2. POST /v1/ingest/batches. schema_version '1.0'.

batch_id.description: Client-generated, unique per attempt-set. A retry of the same batch reuses the same batch_id (idempotency key).

data_plane_id.description: Must match the data_plane_id the presented API key is registered to; the ingest API rejects a mismatch rather than trusting this value blindly.

connector_type.description: e.g. 'postgres', 's3'. Extensible - new connector types require no envelope change.

schema_version.description: Currently '1.0' (shared.schema.CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION). Deliberately not a JSON Schema const here - the ingest API checks the exact supported version in code (control-plane/api/ingest/service.py) and returns a dedicated 'unsupported_schema_version' error, rather than a generic schema-validation failure, so a future minor-version bump is a one-constant change, not a shared/schema edit.

urn.description: Stable identity of the entity across pushes, e.g. urn:postgres:{host}:{database}:{schema}.{table}.

entity_type.description: Selects which shared/schema/<entity_type>.schema.json validates `payload`. Deliberately NOT an enum here - architecture.md §2: 'new types don't require an envelope change, only a new schema file'. The MVP set this ingest API can currently dispatch to is shared.schema.ENTITY_SCHEMA_FILES ({table, column, dataset, job, lineage_edge, scrape_run}); an unrecognized value is rejected per-entity as 'unsupported_entity_type' rather than failing the whole envelope, so an old ingest API and a data plane that's started emitting a newer entity_type degrade gracefully (that one entity is rejected, the rest of the batch still processes).

content_hash.description: e.g. 'sha256:...'. Optional - lets the fan-out worker skip re-writing when a re-scrape found no change. Not required for delete operations.

payload.description: Entity-type-specific fields, validated against shared/schema/<entity_type>.schema.json. For operation=delete this may be an empty object - only urn/entity_type are needed to tombstone.
